request.what: Fund Tx3 by TxPipe as an open API layer for Cardano dApp protocols, including standardized protocol interfaces, documentation, multi-language SDKs, live JSON-RPC endpoints, agent-first documentation, protocol skills, and an MCP server.

claims.claim: The proposal requests 1,308,000 ADA plus a 327,000 ADA contingency reserve over 12 months, while the on-chain withdrawal and budget summary total 1,684,050 ADA including a 49,050 ADA administration fee.
The proposer claims there is currently no common interface mechanism across the Cardano ecosystem, forcing integrators to relearn each protocol and rebuild understanding independently.

Tx3 is described as a framework where each protocol is described once with a verified interface definition that produces documentation, auto-generated SDKs in multiple languages, and live JSON-RPC endpoints.
The proposer claims Catalyst Fund 14 has already put the Tx3 developer layer into production with 5 protocols live on the Tx3 Protocol Registry.
The proposal funds 12 additional protocol onboardings, 3 per quarter, plus MCP server and skill framework development as shared infrastructure for all protocols on the registry.
The proposer claims the proposal achieved the required 67% support threshold during the 2026 Intersect Budget Process Hydra Voting phase.
The proposer claims the requested amount does not breach the applicable 350M ADA Net Change Limit for Epoch 613 to Epoch 713 at the time of submission.
Audit and oversight costs are said to be included in the overhead, with Intersect and technically capable third parties providing reporting obligations and milestone-based disbursement controls.

TxPipe is stated to have received funding through 30 Project Catalyst proposals across Funds 9 through 14, with 26 delivered and 4 under development and on schedule, plus 2025 Intersect open-source maintenance funding delivered on schedule.

Intersect will administer funds through Sundae Labs treasury management smart contracts with specified TRSC and PSSC addresses, role-based authorization thresholds, an oversight committee, and a public dashboard for auditability.

summary: The document describes a 1,684,050 ADA treasury withdrawal for TxPipe's Tx3 open API layer, with claimed ecosystem integration benefits, 12-month deliverables, Intersect process approval, NCL compliance, and smart-contract-based fund administration, but the deterministic assessment reports missing complete summary, budget, feasibility, risk, alternatives, and failure-mode analysis.
